title: Measure of set imaginarity
authors: Yu Guo, Jiabo Pan, Yuqin Wang, Shuanping Du
abstract: Recent studies have shown that Bargmann invariants provide effective detectors of set imaginarity. In this paper, we investigate set imaginarity as a quantum resource in qubit systems. By exploiting the structure of Bargmann invariants, we show that the free operations for qubit set imaginarity consist precisely of common unital operations and common planarized operations. Based on this characterization, we introduce an axiomatic framework for set-imaginarity measures (SIMs). In particular, we propose two refined notions, namely unified SIMs and complete SIMs, which allow a more fine-grained quantification of set imaginarity. To make these notions concrete, we construct two qubit SIMs from the Bargmann invariants of three-state subsets. We prove that one of them is a unified SIM, while the other satisfies the stronger requirements of a complete SIM. Furthermore, we revisit the robustness of set imaginarity previously introduced in the literature. We show that, although this robustness is a valid SIM for qubit systems, it is neither a unified SIM nor a complete SIM. To overcome this limitation, we propose an improved robustness-type measure and rigorously prove that it defines a complete qubit SIM.
summary: This paper introduces the concept of 'set imaginarity' as a quantum resource and develops a formal axiomatic theory for quantifying it via Set Imaginarity Measures (SIMs). Using tools like Bargmann invariants, the authors characterize the free operations for qubit set imaginarity and propose refined, mathematically rigorous measures that improve upon existing definitions.
main_problem: The paper investigates 'set imaginarity' as a quantum resource in qubit systems and develops an axiomatic framework for quantifying this resource.
main_result: The free operations for qubit set imaginarity are characterized by common unital and planarized operations, leading to the proposal of unified and complete Set Imaginarity Measures (SIMs).
method: The authors utilize Bargmann invariants and analyze the properties of quantum channels acting on sets of states to define and test candidate measures.
model_or_system: The focus is on qubit systems ($d=2$) and generalizations to qudit systems ($S(d)$), analyzing sets of quantum states $\vec{ho} = \{ho_j\}$.
key_observables: Set imaginarity ($\check{I}(\vec{ho})$), Bargmann invariants ($\Delta_n(\vec{ho})$), and the Bloch vector representation of the states.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the system ($d$), the number of states in the set ($n$), and the structure of the quantum channel $E$.
main_assumptions: The resource theory framework is extended from single states to sets of states, acknowledging that the set of imaginarity-free states is generally non-convex.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical significance of set imaginarity using Bargmann invariants, then defining the axiomatic requirements for a SIM (SI1-SI5), constructing specific SIMs for qubits, and finally proposing improved measures for higher dimensions.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, axiomatic framework for quantifying a non-standard quantum resource (set imaginarity), which is crucial for understanding collective quantum properties beyond single-state measures.
